scope.goal: Replace the explicit Inventory transaction lifecycle with capability-specific outbox ports, migrate all Inventory event-producing stock commands to atomic state/outbox persistence, add explicit retention configuration, and record the dual-broadcast and source-deletion boundaries.
scope.target: Inventory Application/Infrastructure outbox slice, broker-free tests, architecture/requirements/specifications, operations docs, and workflow evidence
constraints: Application depends on outbox capabilities; local transaction or Unit of Work remains an Infrastructure detail.
DecreaseStock, IncreaseStock, Restock, and successful ReserveInventory state plus event intent commit atomically.
InitProductStock remains without an invented integration event.
Published Inventory outbox rows default to unlimited retention with one validated configuration path.
Kafka plus RabbitMQ dual broadcast is a target direction, but no active claim is allowed before destination-aware delivery state and fanout routing exist.
External-service tests remain opt-in and skipped results are never passing evidence.
Original-source deletion is repository-owner-only and prohibited for AI execution.
non_goals: Implement RabbitMQ exchange bindings, per-consumer queues, or dual-destination publisher routing in this slice.
Add an integration event to InitProductStock.
Delete source, push, open a pull request, merge, close Issue #2, or publish.

architecture_decisions: Transactional Outbox is the Application-visible capability; Unit of Work is an optional private adapter mechanism.
All Inventory commands that emit integration events use source outbox.
RetainAll is the default Inventory published-row retention policy.
Kafka plus RabbitMQ dual broadcast requires independent destination state and remains unimplemented.
user_constraints: Prefer outbox over a broadly exposed Unit of Work for the current architecture.
Do not limit retention now, but make the adjustment location explicit.
Adopt the source-outbox recommendation for other applicable Inventory commands.
Treat dual broadcast as the likely direction.
Do not delete source; only the owner may do so.

approval_contract.required_before: production architecture, specification, source, configuration, and test changes

finding_evidence: DecreaseStock, IncreaseStock, and Restock saved the aggregate before direct broker publication.
ReserveInventory exposed Begin, Stage, and Commit through Application transaction interfaces.
InventoryIntegrationOutbox had one PublishedAt and therefore could not represent two broker destinations independently.
acceptance_criteria: No Inventory event-producing use case directly publishes after save.
Application exposes IInventoryReservationOutbox and IInventoryStockOutbox, not a generic Unit of Work or explicit transaction lifecycle.
PostgreSQL ordinary stock updates use expected-stock optimistic concurrency and stage the outgoing event in the same local transaction.
Relay supports decreased, increased, and returned event types with stable ProductId partition keys.
Retention defaults to RetainAll and finite retention fails fast without positive days.
Dual-broadcast prerequisites, concrete consumer ownership examples, and owner-only source deletion are durable and unambiguous.

steps: Record the Outbox versus Unit of Work decision and the dual-destination prerequisite.
Replace the reservation transaction lifecycle with an atomic outbox port.
Move decrease, increase, and restock from direct publication to atomic stock/outbox persistence.
Add validated retention configuration and relay message-type coverage.
Update reconstruction specs, consumer ownership examples, and owner-only deletion boundary.
Run focused and full validation without counting skipped external checks as passing.

RabbitMQ exchange, queue, binding, DLQ, and Wolverine dual-publisher routing.
Real PostgreSQL atomicity/concurrency proof for ordinary stock commands.

results.summary: Replaced the Application-visible reservation transaction lifecycle with capability-specific outbox ports, migrated all current Inventory event-producing commands to atomic state/outbox persistence, added explicit RetainAll configuration, and documented dual-broadcast prerequisites and owner-only source deletion. Broker-free validation passes; PostgreSQL proof and the unchanged 100% gate remain open.
